title: Borealis Inference Cost Retrofit Proposal
content:
Purpose and context:

This is a working draft analysis for Borealis Analytics — a mid-market analytics vendor currently running mixed real-time and async LLM workloads. The goal: show a concrete before/after cost and latency picture after applying Redwood Optimize recommendations and a small Dedicated commitment for peak capacity. This is intended for the customer success review and the solutions engineering handoff.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Baseline monthly inference spend (current): $78,400
- Proposed Redwood Optimize + small Dedicated reservation: estimated monthly spend after changes: $48,900
- Estimated gross savings: $29,500 / month (~37.6% reduction)
- Key levers: model variant alignment, 8-bit quantization + perf-tested kernels, prefix/KV caching on chat flows, workload-aware batching, reserved capacity for predictable throughput.

Important caveats:
- Baseline numbers supplied by Borealis billing CSV (Q3+Q4) and interviews; we sampled representative request traces but did not get full token-level telemetry for all routes. Realized savings will vary by chat/embedding traffic mix and peak concurrency assumptions.
- Security/regulatory constraint: ~18% of traffic contains regulated PII and must remain in-region (EU). Those requests cannot be routed to cheapest regions but can still benefit from quantization and caching where allowed.

Baseline assumptions and breakdown (customer-provided):
- Monthly requests: 1.35M total requests (mix: 55% chat/classic gen, 30% embeddings, 15% reranking/other).
- Avg tokens/request: chat: 420 (prompt+response), embedding: 1,024 tokens (per item batch), rerank: 180 tokens.
- Current model mix: hosted-llama-65b (for 60% of chat), gptx-13b (30% of chat), embeddings: embed-large-v1.
- Current average latency SLOs: 250–600 ms for interactive chat; embeddings latency 80–200 ms.
- Current delivery: all hosted, no reserved capacity. Occasional throttling in peak windows.

Baseline monthly cost (reconciled from billing export):
- Token generation (chat & rerank): $46,700
- Embeddings: $21,500
- Misc (routing, egress, storage for KV cache): $10,200
- Total: $78,400

Redwood Optimize recommendations (proposed stack and configuration):
1) Model alignment and pruning:
   - Replace hosted-llama-65b with rex-22b-8q (Redwood-validated 8-bit variant) for 60% of chat traffic where long context >2k is not required. Retain llama-like 65b for very long-context customers but at lower traffic share.
   - Replace gptx-13b with gptx-13b-8bit for 100% of remaining chat traffic after perf testing.
   - Move embeddings from embed-large-v1 -> embed-mid-quant (40% cheaper, equivalent quality on Borealis prompts after A/B eval).

2) Quantization and kernel tuning:
   - Enable 8-bit quantization profiles with validated kernels on Dedicated GPU pools. Expect 2.2–2.7x throughput improvement per GPU equivalent for chat workloads.

3) Caching and prefix KV:
   - Implement prefix caching for user-system prompts and common instruction templates. Conservative estimate: 12% request token reduction on chat (prefix tokens removed from runtime).
   - Enable KV cache reuse for session continuity — reduces decode cost for multi-turn sessions by ~18% (customer session length distribution used).

4) Batching and autoscaling policy tweaks:
   - For async embedding jobs: use batch size 96 with per-job windowing to trade latency for throughput. Estimated embedding cost drop by 28% on batchable traffic.
   - For interactive routes: continuous-aware batching with max latency SLO guard (250 ms) — expected small latency increase under <5% of requests during peaks but large throughput gains off-peak.

5) Routing & reserved capacity:
   - Route non-PII, non-SLA-critical inference to lower-cost regions (us-west-3) with automatic fallback to eu-west-1 for regulated requests.
   - Recommend a small Dedicated reservation to cover 65% of peak baseline QPS (3-month ramp). This gives committed unit discounts and avoids spot preemption.

Projected after-optimization cost breakdown (conservative mid-case):
- Chat & rerank generation: $29,200 (down from $46,700) — drivers: model swap + quantization + caching + batching
- Embeddings: $15,400 (down from $21,500) — drivers: batch size + model swap
- Misc (routing overhead, reserved infra): $4,300 (includes Dedicated reservation amortized)
- Total: $48,900

Savings sensitivity matrix (monthly):
- Best case: 45–52% reduction (~$35k–$41k) if embed-mid accuracy passes A/B and caching hits are higher than expected (20%+).
- Mid (presented above): 37.6% reduction (~$29.5k).
- Conservative (lower caching, 8-bit conversion requires fallback for some routes): 20–25% reduction (~$15k–$20k).

Operational impacts and risk assessment:
- Quality risk: Any model variant swap must pass Borealis-specific eval set. We recommend a 3-tier eval: automated metric delta (embedding cosine drift threshold), human eval for top-N cases, and live canary with shadow traffic.
- Latency risk: Continuous batching can add jitter under peak; define per-route SLOs and implement automatic fallback to single-request execution for SLO misses.
- Compliance risk: Ensure all regionally constrained requests are pinned; Redwood Private/Dedicated can be used if Borealis decides to keep all regulated workloads in a VPC.

Implementation plan and timeline (8–10 weeks recommended):
- Week 0–1: finalize eval datasets + acceptance criteria with Borealis (SE + CS workshop).
- Week 2–3: model onboarding + perf benchmarking on replicated workload (redwood infra).
- Week 4: A/B embedding quality test, small-scale canary for quantized models.
- Week 5–6: rollout prefix caching & batch config to non-PII routes; monitor quality and latency.
- Week 7–8: enable Reserved capacity and switch stable traffic over; enable routing policies.
- Week 9–10: stabilization, review cost deltas vs baseline, adjust autoscaling policies.

Measurement plan (KPIs):
- Cost per effective token (pre/post) by route
- 95th/99th latency percentiles for chat and embedding routes
- Embedding vector quality delta (cosine similarity baseline vs new) and downstream retrieval accuracy metric
- Cache hit rate and measured token reduction

Open questions / decisions needed from Borealis:
- Acceptable quality delta thresholds for embeddings (proposed: max 0.6% mAP degradation tolerated)
- Willingness to accept regional routing for non-PII (this enables largest cost wins)
- Appetite for 6–12 month Dedicated reservation (we've modeled a small 6-month commit in numbers above)

Immediate next steps (for internal Redwood):
- SEs: schedule a 90-minute alignment workshop (owners: Owen, Lina).
- Product-optimize: prepare a sandbox eval harness and baseline perf script (owner: Maya).
- CS: draft a short customer-facing one-pager summarizing expected savings and implementation timeline.

Notes / scratch: quick math and assumptions used in spreadsheet (kept here for traceability)
- Baseline token cost rates inferred: chat gen $0.0045 per 1k tokens equivalent average; embeddings $0.021 per embedding call average (based on billing export mixed with unit estimates).
- 8-bit quantization throughput estimate conservative: 2.2x improvement; per-token compute cost scaled accordingly.
- Cache hit assumed 12% on chat prefix tokens; KV reuse assumed 18% reduction for multi-turn flows.

Attachments to produce for final customer packet:
- Detailed XLS with per-route token math, sensitivity tabs (best/mid/worst), and billing reconciliation sheet.
- Eval results export (A/B embedding vectors + metrics).
- Step-by-step runbook for enabling caching and batching hooks in Redwood Console.

——
Rough log: initial draft 2025-11-04 by Maya; discussed with Owen 2025-12-09; Lina added embedding A/B numbers 2026-01-18. Last update: adjusted Dedicated reservation amortization and sensitivity band 2026-02-20.

End of document.
